heading.en: Where does the heat go when a gas is warmed?

hook.en: Heat a gas in a cylinder with a free piston. Part of the heat makes the gas hotter and part pushes the piston out. Energy is never lost, only shared.
hook.kn: ಮುಕ್ತ ಪಿಸ್ಟನ್ ಇರುವ ಸಿಲಿಂಡರ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಅನಿಲ ಬಿಸಿಮಾಡಿ. ಉಷ್ಣದ ಒಂದು ಭಾಗ ಅನಿಲವನ್ನು ಬಿಸಿಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ, ಇನ್ನೊಂದು ಭಾಗ ಪಿಸ್ಟನ್ ತಳ್ಳುತ್ತದೆ. ಶಕ್ತಿ ನಾಶವಾಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

say.en: Heat a gas in a cylinder with a free piston. Part of the heat makes the gas hotter and part pushes the piston out. Energy is never lost, only shared. In this lesson: State and apply the first law delta Q equals delta U plus delta W.
Relate Cp and Cv: Cp - Cv equals R.

body.en: Heat ΔQ supplied to a system goes partly into raising its internal energy ΔU and partly into work ΔW done by the system: ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW. It is the law of conservation of energy. Sign convention: ΔQ is positive when heat is given to the system, ΔW is positive when the system does work.
body.kn: ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆಗೆ ನೀಡಿದ ಉಷ್ಣ ΔQ ಆಂತರಿಕ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚಳ ΔU ಮತ್ತು ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆ ಮಾಡಿದ ಕೆಲಸ ΔW ಆಗಿ ಹಂಚಿಕೆಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ: ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW. ಇದು ಶಕ್ತಿ ಸಂರಕ್ಷಣೆ.

points.en: ΔQ > 0: heat given to the system
ΔW > 0: work done by the system

narration.kn: ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆಗೆ ನೀಡಿದ ಉಷ್ಣ ΔQ ಆಂತರಿಕ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚಳ ΔU ಮತ್ತು ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆ ಮಾಡಿದ ಕೆಲಸ ΔW ಆಗಿ ಹಂಚಿಕೆಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ: ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW. ಇದು ಶಕ್ತಿ ಸಂರಕ್ಷಣೆ.

say.en: Heat delta Q supplied to a system goes partly into raising its internal energy delta U and partly into work delta W done by the system: delta Q equals delta U plus delta W. It is the law of conservation of energy. Sign convention: delta Q is positive when heat is given to the system, delta W is positive when the system does work. delta Q is greater than 0: heat given to the system.
say.kn: ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆಗೆ ನೀಡಿದ ಉಷ್ಣ delta Q ಆಂತರಿಕ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚಳ delta U ಮತ್ತು ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆ ಮಾಡಿದ ಕೆಲಸ delta W ಆಗಿ ಹಂಚಿಕೆಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ: delta Q equals delta U plus delta W. ಇದು ಶಕ್ತಿ ಸಂರಕ್ಷಣೆ.

say.en: delta W is greater than 0: work done by the system.
Draw the system as a box. Heat Q flows in; the system does work W on its surroundings; the rest raises its internal energy.
Energy is conserved: heat supplied equals the rise in internal energy plus the work done by the system.
If 500 joule of heat goes in and the gas does 200 joule of work, the internal energy rises by 300 joule.
At constant volume no work is done, so all the heat raises U. At constant pressure, some heat also does work P ΔV.

draw.tex: V\text{ const: } Q = \mu C_v\Delta T = \Delta U
P\text{ const: } Q = \mu C_v\Delta T + P\Delta V

say.en: For an ideal gas P ΔV is mu R ΔT. So C_p is bigger than C_v by exactly R: Mayer's relation.

draw.tex: \mu C_p\Delta T = \mu C_v\Delta T + \mu R\Delta T

say.en: Their ratio is gamma: five thirds for a monatomic gas, seven fifths for a diatomic one.

narration.en: Heat Q given to a gas is shared: ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW. With the piston pinned (constant volume) no work is done and all of it raises the internal energy. With the piston free (constant pressure) part of it pushes the piston out, so the temperature rises less: that is why Cp = Cv + R.
narration.kn: ಅನಿಲಕ್ಕೆ ಕೊಟ್ಟ ಉಷ್ಣ ಹಂಚಿಕೆಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ: ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW. ಪಿಸ್ಟನ್ ಬಂಧಿಸಿದರೆ (ಸ್ಥಿರ ಗಾತ್ರ) ಕೆಲಸ ಇಲ್ಲ, ಎಲ್ಲವೂ ಆಂತರಿಕ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಏರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪಿಸ್ಟನ್ ಮುಕ್ತವಾದರೆ (ಸ್ಥಿರ ಒತ್ತಡ) ಒಂದು ಭಾಗ ಪಿಸ್ಟನ್ ತಳ್ಳುತ್ತದೆ, ತಾಪ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಏರುತ್ತದೆ: ಹಾಗಾಗಿ Cp = Cv + R.

title.en: Specific heat capacities of a gas

body.en: A gas has two molar *specific heats*: Cv at constant volume (no work done, all heat raises U) and Cp at constant pressure (some heat does work). For an ideal gas Cp − Cv = R (Mayer's relation), so Cp > Cv. Their ratio γ = Cp/Cv is 5/3 for a monatomic gas and 7/5 for a diatomic gas.
body.kn: ಅನಿಲಕ್ಕೆ ಸ್ಥಿರ ಗಾತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ Cv ಮತ್ತು ಸ್ಥಿರ ಒತ್ತಡದಲ್ಲಿ Cp. ಆದರ್ಶ ಅನಿಲಕ್ಕೆ Cp − Cv = R. γ = Cp/Cv.

narration.en: A gas has two molar specific heats: Cv at constant volume (no work done, all heat raises U) and Cp at constant pressure (some heat does work). For an ideal gas Cp − Cv = R (Mayer's relation), so Cp > Cv. Their ratio γ = Cp/Cv is 5/3 for a monatomic gas and 7/5 for a diatomic gas.

say.en: A gas has two molar specific heats: Cv at constant volume (no work done, all heat raises U) and Cp at constant pressure some heat does work. For an ideal gas Cp - Cv equals R (Mayer's relation), so Cp is greater than Cv. Their ratio gamma equals Cp over Cv is 5 over 3 for a monatomic gas and 7 over 5 for a diatomic gas.

say.en: gamma equals Cp over Cv: 5 over 3 monatomic, 7 over 5 diatomic.

problem.en: A gas absorbs 800 J of heat and does 500 J of work. Find the change in its internal energy.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A gas absorbs 800 J of heat and does 500 J of work. Find the change in its internal energy.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A gas absorbs 800 joules of heat and does 500 joules of work. Find the change in its internal energy.
delta U equals delta Q - delta W.
delta U equals 800 minus 500 = plus 300 joules internal energy rises.
So the answer is plus 300 joules.

problem.en: 2 mol of a monatomic ideal gas (Cv = 3R/2) are heated at constant volume through 10 K. Find the heat supplied. (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)

steps.en: Q ≈ 249 J; all of it raises U since no work is done.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. 2 mol of a monatomic ideal gas (Cv = 3R/2) are heated at constant volume through 10 K. Find the heat supplied. (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)

say.en: Let us solve this together. 2 moles of a monatomic ideal gas (Cv equals 3R/2) are heated at constant volume through 10 kelvin. Find the heat supplied. (R equals 8.31 joules mol to the power minus 1 K to the power minus 1).
Q equals micro Cvdelta T equals 2 times 1.5 times 8.31 times 10.
Q is approximately 249 joules; all of it raises U since no work is done.
So the answer is About 249 joules.
